title: set(cat_features) rebuilt once per feature inside the list-comprehension filter
description: `continuous = [f for f in features if f not in set(cat_features)]` places set(cat_features) in the comprehension's filter predicate, which CPython re-evaluates for every element of `features` — rebuilding the set O(len(features)) times instead of once. Hoisting the set out of the comprehension (compute `cat_set = set(cat_features)` once, then `[f for f in features if f not in cat_set]`) preserves behaviour exactly and makes the membership test O(1) against a single set. The codebase already uses this hoisted idiom elsewhere (e.g. _auto_terms line 48 `cat_set = set(cat_features)`, _algorithms.py:276).
evidence: Line 481: `continuous = [f for f in features if f not in set(cat_features)]`. The expression `set(cat_features)` is part of the `if` clause, so it is constructed afresh on each iteration of `f in features`; the result is identical every time. Compare _auto_terms (line 48-49) which correctly binds `cat_set = set(cat_features)` once before the loop.
est_reduction: 0 net LOC (1 line hoisted into 1 binding + 1 use); removes a per-element set rebuild — micro-perf + consistency with the established cat_set idiom
behavior_preservation: Identical output: f not in set(cat_features) and f not in cat_set are equivalent for every f; only the number of times the set is built changes. No ordering, dtype, or value change.
